catholic-encyclopedia-1913-the-slavs:
Peoples now called Slavs, a name that surfaced late yet displaced all rivals, are surveyed here in origin, language, and history. Written documents first show the name in the sixth century. Ptolemy, about 100 to 178, already noted tribes in Sarmatia that Safarik links to Slavs: Stavani in European Sarmatia and Soubenoi across the Alani in Asia. 

Poor copyists' spelling, Ptolemy drawing on two sources, may explain the double naming of one people. Divisions into eastern, western, and southern Slavs follow, with languages, migrations, conversions, and states. For readers seeking the Slav world in one sweep, the entry maps a vast family from its first mentions to modern nations.
doe-osti-2587134-decision-tree-for-varia:
Alvina Aui, Mengyao Yuan, and Wenqin Li of Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory, with Allegra Mayer and Anne Ware of the National Renewable Energy Laboratory, presented these slides in October 2025 as LLNL-TR-2010490. The deck builds a decision tree for two carbon removal paths: burying biomass, and burying biochar made from biomass. Both aim to lock carbon away for a long time.

Durability is the hard question, since these lower-readiness pathways have little long-term field data behind them. The tree sorts outcomes into bands: low durability means major reversal of storage, moderate means the carbon stays put for 100 to 1,000 years, and high means more than 1,000 years. Variables such as the hydrogen-to-organic-carbon ratio and random reflectance, a measure of aromatic structure, help judge where a project lands. The authors flag the bands as relative guides that need more data for validation.
doe-osti-3024762-accelerated-selectrion-:
Alex Zunger of the University of Colorado Boulder reports award DE-EE0009515, running October 2021 through August 2025, on picking better perovskite alloys for solar cells. Halide perovskites are promising light absorbers with a huge chemical space, far too many candidate mixes to test one by one. The project combined quantum calculations with machine learning in a hierarchy, screening broadly first and spending heavy computation only on survivors.

A thread of the work concerns a descriptor, called tau, that classifies whether a compound will form a stable perovskite from its composition alone. Screening tools of this kind were also aimed at light-emitting diodes and photocatalysis in the group's related publications. The final report form covers the last budget period, October 2023 to August 2025, inside the full project span.
doe-osti-3028682-parallel-processed-mult:
David P Fenning of the University of California, San Diego, led award DE-EE0009521, from October 2021 to March 2025, on multi-junction perovskite solar cells made by parallel processing. Stacking perovskite junctions lets a cell harvest more of the spectrum, but every interface in the stack is a place the device can later split apart. The report therefore measures toughness alongside efficiency.

Thermal cycling got a clear answer. Control device stacks showed average interfacial toughness of 0.27 joules per square meter, plus or minus 0.08, while stacks put through fifty thermal cycles measured 0.20, plus or minus 0.04. Each figure rests on four measurements across two substrates. The drop sits inside the statistical uncertainty, so the authors conclude cycling had minimal impact on the toughness of these stacks.
podcast-dannyjones--T38tBm54vs:
Tim Hogan studies the Knights Templar, the medieval order of warrior monks dissolved in the early 1300s amid charges many historians call manufactured. On Danny Jones's podcast, Hogan argues that the Vatican is hiding the bones of Jesus Christ, and that Templar secrets sit at the center of the alleged cover-up.

Hogan lays out his reading of the order's history and the relics he believes the Church controls. Jones presses him through the chain of claims, from medieval trials to modern Vatican secrecy. The episode states a fringe theory in its strongest form, and listeners get the full argument from a believer rather than a summary from a critic. It is kept here as the guest presented it, without endorsement.
